summary: Pattern matches in @solana-labs/web3.js bundle require manual verification
details: The package ships bundled CommonJS and ESM builds (lib/index.cjs.js, lib/index.esm.js) that contain co-occurring keywords typical of an HTTP client library: fetch() calls, an https.get reference, POST literals, and the token 'ping'. These shapes are also consistent with the documented purpose of the package — a Solana JSON-RPC client and websocket helper that performs HTTP POSTs to user-configured RPC endpoints and exposes a 'ping' RPC method. No network destinations were extracted from the matched lines; the patterns alone do not establish an attacker-controlled endpoint, install-time execution, credential reads, or exfiltration of installer data. Tracing of the minified bundle did not complete, so the call sites were not semantically verified. Routing to human review so a reviewer can confirm whether the fetch/https.get call sites resolve to user-supplied RPC URLs (benign SDK behavior) or to hardcoded destinations (which would warrant escalation).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
